statement: Stream Grasshopper curves, surfaces, breps and meshes to connected mixed-reality devices without baking them into the document.
superiority: Delta streaming of changed objects only, with LOD and mesh compression for large models.

acceptance.corpus: 10,000-face brep model edited 30 times/s via slider
acceptance.tolerance: Device receives each update <= 100 ms on LAN; payload <= 20% of full mesh

statement: Give synced objects colours and materials suitable for the device, noting one-sided shading and black displaying as transparent.
superiority: Native PBR materials with preview that matches the headset rendering.

acceptance.tolerance: Preview matches device render within DeltaE 5

statement: Move, rotate and scale already-synced objects by sending only a transform instead of re-sending geometry.
superiority: Transform animation at display refresh rate with interpolation on device.

acceptance.tolerance: Bandwidth per frame <= 64 bytes/object; no geometry resend

statement: Mark synced objects as clickable, moveable or grabbable so users can interact with them on the device and receive events.
superiority: Events delivered with device id and timestamp, usable in any definition.

acceptance.corpus: 100 interactive objects, 200 click events from 2 devices
acceptance.tolerance: All events received once; device ids correct

statement: Expose sliders, toggles, buttons and value lists to the device so changing them there updates the Grasshopper document and vice versa.
superiority: No per-file parameter cap and two-way conflict resolution.

acceptance.tolerance: Last-writer-wins converges <= 200 ms; no lost updates

statement: Report which device changed a synced parameter so definitions can respond per user.
superiority: Per-user attribution and audit log of changes.

acceptance.corpus: 3 devices changing the same slider alternately
acceptance.tolerance: Correct device id on 100% of changes

statement: Let several headsets and phones on the same network view and use the same live model together.
superiority: Discover and join over LAN or cloud without manual network setup.

acceptance.tolerance: All clients converge to same state within 300 ms after each edit

statement: Connect a device to the running Rhino session before the Grasshopper components start streaming, and recover from lost connections.
superiority: Automatic reconnect that resumes sync without re-opening the document.

acceptance.tolerance: Session resumes <= 5 s each time; no stale geometry

statement: Make curves visible on the device, where raw curves are not shown by default, by converting them to a displayable form.
superiority: Native thick-line rendering of curves without geometry conversion.

acceptance.tolerance: All displayed with width within 5% of requested

statement: Align the virtual model with the physical site or workshop using marker or reference points so elements can be positioned from the hologram.
superiority: Multi-point alignment solved with residual report.

statement: Measure how accurately holographic guidance and a physical build agree and report the deviation.
superiority: Per-element deviation heat map from scan data.

acceptance.corpus: Synthetic as-built points with 5 mm random offsets
acceptance.tolerance: Deviations reported within 0.5 mm of truth

statement: Show components of a design step by step on the device to guide manual assembly in a workshop.
superiority: Step sequencing from a schedule with completion tracking.

acceptance.tolerance: Each step shows correct part; progress saved
